rationale: Prolangs-C++/life is a tiny, loop-heavy cellular-automata simulation with a small hot kernel (neighbor counting and grid update), and the empty static profile indicates no large function bodies or deep call graphs to protect structurally. The goal is therefore data/flow-level confusion in the hot loops rather than structural passes: FLA and BCF get high SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights because control-flow flattening and bogus branches most disrupt static analysis of the small loop nest, but their RuntimeCost weights are kept moderate-to-high (0.6/0.4) so the selector avoids applying them where the profile suggests per-cell inner loops would suffer disproportionate overhead. SUB is cheap and correct with strong local hiding of the neighbor-count arithmetic, so it gets low cost penalties and solid gain weights. SPLIT and IBR are inexpensive enablers that improve diversity and hamper diffing with near-zero runtime impact, so they are kept active with mild weights. ICALL is restrained (CorrectnessRisk 0.4, RuntimeCost 0.5) because indirect-call dispatch in a C++ program's small hot functions adds virtual-dispatch-style overhead and can stress exception/ABI assumptions with limited payoff on such a small binary. IGV is kept low across dimensions: with no significant global-variable surface evident and a small data section, its gains are marginal and its interprocedural variable-remapping carries nontrivial correctness risk in C++ code.
